finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: Receiving more data than the size of the packet buffer
finding.assumptions: The packet buffer size is fixed at 4096 bytes, and the received data size is not checked against this limit.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the recvfrom call on line 41: the third argument is sizeof(packet), which is 4096. The recvfrom function guarantees that it will write at most that many bytes into the buffer, so no overflow can occur regardless of the amount of data received. No additional checks are needed.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: Printing untrusted data without proper sanitization
finding.assumptions: The values of field1 and field2 are directly printed without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the sink is printf, which does not execute OS commands. The source values field1 and field2 are numeric (uint16_t and uint32_t) and are converted via ntohs/ntohl before printing. Since printf only outputs formatted text, there is no command execution path. Therefore OS Command Injection cannot occur.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.trigger: Using untrusted data in socket creation parameters
finding.assumptions: The parameters for socket creation are not validated or sanitized.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the socket creation call at line 22. The arguments AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, and IPPROTO_RAW are compile‑time constants, not derived from any user‑controlled input such as stdin, argv, environment variables, or network data. Therefore the source of untrusted data is not present, and no path exists from an untrusted source to the socket call. No OS command injection is possible.
